estados.title: States to extract
estados.description: Which process states to fetch. AP = upcoming openings, ET = in progress, CO = concluded/awarded.

fetchDetail.title: Fetch full detail per process
fetchDetail.description: When enabled (default), fetches each process's detail page for full description, rubros, organism and direct document links (pliego, resolucion, etc). Disable for a faster, listing-only run.

maxItems.title: Max processes to extract
maxItems.description: Hard cap on the number of processes returned this run, across all selected states.

onlyNew.title: Delta mode - only new processes since last run
onlyNew.description: When enabled, persists seen process ids between runs (in this actor's own key-value store, per estado) and returns only processes not seen in a prior run. NOTE: this source's listing order is not reliably newest-first (AP is sorted by soonest-opening-date, not recency; ET/CO show no correlation between position and id or date at all - verified live), so pagination always walks the full listing up to maxItems as it does today, and the unseen-only filter is applied after that fetch rather than short-circuiting it early. Recommended for recurring monitoring; leave off for a full one-off extraction.

dateRange.title: Filter by recency (opening date)
dateRange.description: Optionally restrict results to processes whose own fechaHoraApertura (bid opening date/time) falls within this window of now. Independent of onlyNew - note this is a scheduling date, not a publication date: for AP (upcoming openings) it's necessarily in the future, so this answers 'opening in the next Nh/d', not 'discovered in the last Nh/d'. onlyNew is the more reliable 'what's new' signal for recurring monitoring; use this when you specifically want the source's own opening-date semantics.
